Ltd on 3 January, 2023 In The Court Of Ms. Barkha Gupta, District Judge (Commercial Court), North-East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi C.S. (Comm) No. 15/2021 Cnr No. Dlne01-000282-2021 Sh. Prehlad Rai Garg, Proprietor of 'M/s P.N.D. Masala Company', At K-216, Karawal Nagar, Delhi. Also At - C-245, Sector-4, Bawana, Delhi. Versus M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd., Through its Director, Plot No. 736 Ep, Place City-II, Sector-37, Gurugram, Haryana-122001. Date of Institution : 12.01.2021 Final arguments : 21.12.2022 Date of decision : 03.01.2023 Judgment
texts.facts: 1. The plaintiff namely Sh. Prehlad Rai Garg, who is the proprietor of 'M/s P.N.D. Masala Company' (hereinafter referred to as the 'plaintiff') has filed a suit against the defendant 'M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd.' (hereinafter referred to as the 'defendant') through its Director for recovery of a sum of Rs.11,11,750.13 (Rupees Eleven Lakhs Eleven Thousand Seven Hundred Fifty and Thirteen Paise Only) alongwith pendente-lite C.S. (Comm.) 15/2021 Rai Garg vs. M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd. page 1 of 26 and future interest @ 18% per annum alongwith costs of the litigation. 2. Brief facts of the case as revealed from the plaint are that the plaintiff is engaged in the business of supplying cooking masalas to the customers as per their orders. Further, during the regular course of business, the defendant approached the plaintiff and placed orders with him to supply the cooking masalas to it from time to time and thereafter, the plaintiff started supplying the same to the defendant on 'Credit basis', vide various invoices, which were duly accepted and acknowledged by the defendant. He also stated that the defendant also assured him that the bills would cleared periodically. Sh. Prehlad Rai Garg vs M/S Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd on 3 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97497040/ 1 The plaintiff submit that as per the Statement of Account maintained by him, the defendant has to pay him a sum of Rs.7,74,738.77/- excluding interest as on 01.08.2018. 3. The plaintiff submit that he repeatedly requested the defendant to pay the outstanding amount, but the defendant kept on prolonging it on one pretext or the other and hence, the plaintiff sent it a legal notice dated 09.09.2020, vide which, he requested the defendant to pay him the outstanding amount of Rs.11,92,108.15/-, which included the principal amount as well as interest till the date of sending the legal notice, which also included other miscellaneous expenses. He further submit that despite receiving the said notice, the defendant neither gave him C.S. (Comm.) 15/2021 Sh. Prehlad Rai Garg vs. M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd. page 2 of 26 any reply nor made the payment. 4. The plaintiff prays that decree in sum of Rs.11,11,750.13/- (Rs. Eleven Lakhs Eleven Thousand Seven Hundred Fifty and Thirteen Paise Only) alongwith pendente-lite and future interest @ 18% per annum may be passed in his favour and against the defendant from the date of filing of the suit till realization and further prays that the defendant may also be directed to pay him a sum of Rs. 1,25,000/- towards litigation/professional charges/expenses. 5. The defendant, in the written statement has inter alia contended that it is in the business of supplying food to various companies for their workers. Further, FSSAI, Department of Food and Drug Administration Haryana issued it a valid Certificate/License No.10818005000341, however, the plaintiff does not have the requisite valid license under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). 6. The plaintiff, in support of his case, examined himself as PW-1, his son namely Shri Pankaj Garg as PW-2 and Shri R.K. Bhaskar, (Designated Officer, Department of Food Safety, District North East, Delhi) as PW-3. The defendant examined its Managing Director namely Shri Dharmindra Singh as DW-1. 11. From the perusal of record, it is shown on record that the plaintiff also examined Shri R.K. Bhaskar, (Designated Officer, Department of Food Safety, District North East, Delhi) as PW-3, who proved that the Food License bearing no. 13315004000103 was issued by the department to the plaintiff on 30.12.2015, which was valid till 29.12.2020. The plaintiff Shri Prehlad Rai Garg, who is the proprietor of 'M/s PND Masala Company' examined himself as PW-1 and testified vide his affidavit Ex. PW1/A bearing his signatures at points A and B respectively. 19. During cross-examination, the plaintiff/PW1 inter alia stated that he was dealing/doing business with the defendant and his son was handling all the business transactions on his behalf.
texts.arguments: The defendant further submit that since, the plaintiff was in dire need of business, so, he himself approached the defendant at its office at Gurugram, Haryana and submit that it never entered into any contract with the plaintiff as claimed by him and hence, there was no privity of contract between the parties. It also submit that the plaintiff had supplied sub-standard, low quality and old/expired masalas to it. The defendant further submit that when it received various C.S. (Comm.) 15/2021 Sh. Prehlad Rai Garg vs. M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd. page 3 of 26 complaints about the quality of masalas/spices delivered by the plaintiff to it, then, on enquiry, it came to know that the taste of the goods/food supplied by it to various companies was bitter as the plaintiff had supplied low/sub-standard/old/expired quality of the masalas to it. The defendant further submit that the plaintiff was not only negligent in his dealings with the defendant but, the plaintiff was also in connivance with lower staff of the defendant, due to which, the defendant suffered huge losses in its business as its old customers not only lost faith in it but, they also cancelled their contracts with the defendant. 7. The defendant also submit that it never acknowledged any dues towards the plaintiff and allege that plaintiff himself is the wrongdoer and cannot take its advantage. 2 The defendant has denied the contentions and allegations levelled by the plaintiff on it and prays that the suit of the plaintiff may be dismissed being devoid of any merits. 8. The plaintiff, in the replication has reiterated the contentions and averments made by him against the defendant as mentioned in the plaint at length, which are not repeated here for the sake of brevity. He further stated that he did not give any Statement of Account to the defendant and volunteered that his son had sent the same to the defendant. He also stated that he is not actively doing the business of the proprietorship concern and has no knowledge about the transactions, which took place between his son and the defendant and further stated that he has no personal knowledge whether any material/masalas was supplied by his son to the defendant. He further stated that he is not aware of the amount, which the defendant gave to his son and has no personal knowledge about the WhatsApp chats between the parties, which are Ex. PW1/3. 21. He also deposed that during course of business, the defendant approached the plaintiff and requested him to supply the masalas to it and thereafter, the plaintiff supplied the same to the defendant as per its orders. He also testified that the defendant has to pay a sum of Rs.7,74,738.77/- excluding interest to the plaintiff as on 01.08.2018 on account of the masalas supplied by plaintiff to the defendant and has further deposed that though, the plaintiff repeatedly requested the defendant to make the due payment, however, the defendant did not pay any heed and so, the plaintiff sent a legal notice dated 09.09.2020 to the defendant, however, the defendant did not reply and further, despite repeated telephonic calls by the plaintiff, the defendant did not pay the outstanding amount. He reiterated in his affidavit Ex.PW-2/A, whatever the plaintiff has mentioned against the defendant in the plaint, which is not repeated here for the sake of brevity. He also relied upon the documents as already proved by the plaintiff (i.e. his father) as Ex.PW1/1 to Ex. During his cross-examination, PW2 stated that he was doing/looking after the business of the plaintiff alongwith his father (i.e. the plaintiff/PW1), who is the proprietor of 'M/s C.S. Ltd on 3 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97497040/ 6 Masalas Company' and further, he was also looking after the marketing activity of the said proprietorship concern and was also maintaining the accounts. He further stated that the document Ex.PW1/2 is not the Statement of Account, but it is Statement of Ledger/Statement of Account pertaining to the defendant and clarified that he is not aware of the difference between the Statement of Account and Statement of Ledger. He admit that he prepared the Statement of Account Ex.PW1/2, the contents of which are correct. He also stated that the defendant is liable to pay the outstanding amount to the plaintiff for the masalas, which the plaintiff had supplied to the defendant as per document Ex. PW1/2. 23. He volunteered that the plaintiff was earlier doing business from address at K-216, Mukund Vihar Road, Karawal Nagar, Delhi-110094 and about two years ago from the date of his deposition, the plaintiff shifted his said business to Bawana. He also stated that the Statement of Account Ex.PW1/2 pertain to the transactions between the parties w.e.f July, 2017 to August, 2018 and emphasized that the entries were immediately made after the business transactions took place between the parties. He also stated that the first transaction between the parties took place on 17.07.2017, when the plaintiff sold spices C.S. (Comm.) 15/2021 Sh. Prehlad Rai Garg vs. M/s Yes Sir Catering Services Pvt. Ltd. page 12 of 26 (i.e. masalas) to the defendant. 24. During further cross examination, he stated that the plaintiff supplied the spices/masalas to the defendant through tempos/rickshaws, however, he did not remember the names of drivers of tempo/rickshaw pullers. He also volunteered that sometimes even Shri Angad Sodhi, who is the son of Shri Dharminder Sodhi, who is the director of the defendant himself used to collect/purchase spices from the factory of plaintiff about 4-5 times on his own also and Shri Dharminder Sodhi also came to the office of plaintiff about 2-4 times to purchase/collect the spices. He further stated that the plaintiff used to take out three printouts of each of the bills and would give the original bill and its duplicate copy to the local tempo driver/rickshaw puller and stated that he use to give/hand over the masalas to the local tempo drivers/ rickshaw pullers amounting to thousands of rupees. He stated that as such, there was no written/signed agreement between the parties and the plaintiff supplied the masalas to the defendant on credit basis as per orders placed by the defendant. 25. He also stated that Shri Angad Sodhi and Shri Dharminder Sodhi also used to collect the spices from the business office of the plaintiff from Karawal Nagar, Delhi, however, he did not take any acknowledgment from them on the bills/invoices. 27. It is wrong to suggest that the defendant had not placed the orders to the plaintiff any form for supply of spices. It is wrong to suggest that I had supplied the spices to the defendant in connivance with the lower rank employees of the defendant company. It is wrong to suggest that when the sub-standard quality of spices came to the knowledge of the Directors of the defendant company, all the transactions were immediately stopped. It is wrong to suggest that w.e.f. 02.02.2018, the defendant asked the plaintiff not to supply spices to the defendant. (Vol. the plaintiff himself stopped supplying spices to the defendant w.e.f. 05.02.2018). The plaintiff did not send any statement of account to the defendant showing the dues against the defendant. The plaintiff telephonically informed the defendant about the dues for supplying of spices to the defendant". 28. During cross-examination, DW-1 inter alia stated that he is one of the directors of defendant and is running the defendant company i.e. 'Yes Sir Catering Services' for the last about 8-9 years and stated that the name of other director is Ms. Gaganjot Sodhi. He also stated that he does not know the plaintiff i.e. 'M/s PND Masala Company' and admit that the plaintiff used to supply masalas to the defendant, but it was without his knowledge as it was in connivance of the plaintiff with the lower ranked employees of the defendant and does not know as to when, the plaintiff started supplying the masalas to the defendant. He also stated that he does not know whether the defendant made any advance payment to the plaintiff and volunteered that it was without his knowledge that the staff of the defendant had made the said payment.
